input_text: On the issue of whether Ana lied to Jim, Jim's statement on cross-examination that he did not believe Ana to be an honest individual.

extraction.input_text: On the issue of whether Ana lied to Jim, Jim's statement on cross-examination that he did not believe Ana to be an honest individual.

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: Jim's statement was made on cross-examination, meaning it was delivered in court rather than out of court. Under FRE 801(c), hearsay requires an out-of-court statement; thus, this element is not met.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) definition of hearsay requires an out-of-court statement.

arguments.text: The statement asserts Jim's personal belief that Ana was not an honest individual, which constitutes an assertion of a declarant's then-existing state of mind or belief. This satisfies the assertion prong of the hearsay definition.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be an assertion by the declarant.
arguments.evidence_span: that he did not believe Ana to be an honest individual

arguments.text: The statement is offered on the issue of whether Ana lied to Jim, indicating it is likely introduced to demonstrate Jim's state of mind, notice, or the effect on him rather than to prove the truth of Ana's dishonesty. Non-truth purposes fall outside the hearsay rule.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) excludes statements offered for purposes other than proving the truth of the matter asserted (e.g., state of mind, notice).
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether Ana lied to Jim
